shared-computer.title: If someone else uses this computer
shared-computer.what: Chrome can keep a list of the pages Spare Key opens. The other person may also see that Spare Key is in Chrome.
shared-computer.why: Running the check where they cannot look keeps it private. A library computer, a friend's device or a work computer they never use are all options.
shared-computer.tech: Spare Key keeps nothing after Chrome closes unless you save it. An optional cleanup removes the pages it opened from Chrome's history.

quick-exit.title: Quick exit
quick-exit.what: Quick exit closes Spare Key at once and shows a weather search instead.
quick-exit.why: If someone walks in, one press hides what you were doing. Everything from this check is cleared from this computer.
quick-exit.tech: Press Esc twice, press Alt+Shift+X, or use the Quick exit button. It clears session storage, closes the tab Spare Key opened, replaces the page you were on, and closes this panel.

hotline.title: The National Domestic Violence Hotline
hotline.what: Trained advocates answer calls and texts all day, every day, for free. You do not have to give your name.
hotline.why: An advocate can help you decide when and how to change things, which is the hardest part of this.
hotline.tech: You can also chat at thehotline.org. Numbers checked on November 21, 2026.

practice.title: The practice check
practice.what: The practice check runs on made-up settings pages for a person called Jordan. Nothing of yours is opened.
practice.why: It shows you every step before you check your own accounts.

nano.title: Gemini Nano
nano.what: Gemini Nano is a small AI model that runs inside Chrome, on this computer.
nano.why: Spare Key uses it to read your settings pages, because those pages name people. What it reads never leaves this computer.
nano.tech: Firebase AI Logic in ONLY_ON_DEVICE mode, with no cloud fallback on purpose. Without Gemini Nano, Spare Key reads pages with code only and says where that is less complete.

cloud.title: Plan help from the cloud
cloud.what: Gemini in Google's cloud helps put your plan in a good order.
cloud.why: It sees only the type of each finding, like "mail is forwarded", and the answers you choose to share. Never names, emails, phone numbers or devices.
cloud.tech: Firebase AI Logic in ONLY_IN_CLOUD mode. Every request is shown word for word under Under the hood, What left this computer. With this off, the plan is made on this computer from Spare Key's steps library.

start.title: What happens when you start
start.what: Chrome asks you to let Spare Key read the sites you ticked. The prompt names only those sites.
start.why: Spare Key then opens each settings page in one tab beside this panel and reads it. It never clicks, changes or saves anything on those pages.
start.tech: The access is requested with chrome.permissions.request for the ticked sites only, and you can remove it any time in Chrome's extension settings.

check-google.devices.title: Devices signed in to your Google account
check-google.devices.what: Spare Key will open your Google account's device page and read the list of signed-in devices.
check-google.devices.why: A phone or computer that is still signed in can read your mail, see where you have been, and change your settings.

check-google.apps.title: Apps that can use your Google account
check-google.apps.what: Spare Key will open the list of apps you gave access to your Google account.
check-google.apps.why: An app with access can read mail or see your location without signing in again.

check-google.recovery.title: Your recovery phone and email
check-google.recovery.what: Spare Key will read the phone number and email address that can reset your password.
check-google.recovery.why: Whoever controls these can take over your account, even after you change your password.

check-google.2sv.title: 2-Step Verification
check-google.2sv.what: Spare Key will read which phones and keys can approve a sign-in to your account.
check-google.2sv.why: A phone on this list that is not yours lets someone else approve their own sign-in.

check-maps.sharing.title: Location sharing
check-maps.sharing.what: Spare Key will read who you share your location with in your Google account.
check-maps.sharing.why: Someone on this list can see where you are right now.

check-gmail.forwarding.title: Gmail forwarding
check-gmail.forwarding.what: Spare Key will open Gmail's forwarding settings and read where your mail is sent.
check-gmail.forwarding.why: Forwarding sends a copy of each new email to someone else.

check-gmail.filters.title: Gmail filters
check-gmail.filters.what: Spare Key will read your Gmail filters.
check-gmail.filters.why: A filter can quietly forward some of your mail, or hide it from your inbox.

check-gmail.delegates.title: People who can open your Gmail
check-gmail.delegates.what: Spare Key will read who has been given access to your Gmail.
check-gmail.delegates.why: Someone given access can read, send and delete your mail.

check-google.family.title: Your Google family group
check-google.family.what: Spare Key will read who is in your Google family group and who manages it.
check-google.family.why: A family manager can see some of what you do, and can stop you buying things.

check-photos.sharing.title: Google Photos partner sharing
check-photos.sharing.what: Spare Key will read who your photos are shared with.
check-photos.sharing.why: Partner sharing can send new photos to someone else as you take them, including where they were taken.

check-amazon.household.title: Your Amazon household
check-amazon.household.what: Spare Key will read who is in your Amazon household.
check-amazon.household.why: People in a household can see what you buy and where it is sent.

check-amazon.devices.title: Devices on your Amazon account
check-amazon.devices.what: Spare Key will read the list of devices on your Amazon account, like an Echo, Kindle or Fire TV.
check-amazon.devices.why: A device you do not have can still show your orders, messages or camera feeds.

check-chrome.extensions.title: Extensions in this browser
check-chrome.extensions.what: Spare Key will list the extensions in this Chrome that can read every page you visit.
check-chrome.extensions.why: An extension like that can see everything you do in Chrome, including this check.
check-chrome.extensions.tech: Uses chrome.management, which Chrome describes as "Manage your apps, extensions, and themes". Spare Key only reads the list. Nothing is sent anywhere.

check-chrome.sync.title: Which account this browser syncs to
check-chrome.sync.what: Spare Key will check which account this Chrome sends your history and passwords to.
check-chrome.sync.why: If it is not your account, someone else may see your browsing and saved passwords.
check-chrome.sync.tech: Uses chrome.identity to read the signed-in profile's email and compares it on this computer. Chrome describes this as "Know your email address".

history-cleanup.title: Remove these pages from history
history-cleanup.what: After the check, Spare Key can remove the pages it opened from Chrome's history.
history-cleanup.why: It cannot hide everything. Google's own My Activity may still list the visits. The other person may also see Spare Key in Chrome. Removing it when you are done helps.
history-cleanup.tech: Uses chrome.history.deleteUrl for exactly the pages the scan opened. Chrome describes this as "Read and change your browsing history".

sent-log.title: What left this computer
sent-log.what: This is everything Spare Key sent to Gemini in the cloud, word for word.
sent-log.why: Names, emails, phone numbers and devices are never in it. You can check that here.
sent-log.tech: Each request is written here before it is sent. It passes a check that allows only finding types and fixed answers, and that refuses anything this check found.

how-check.title: The check
how-check.what: Spare Key opens each of your settings pages in one tab beside its panel, waits for the page, and reads the list on it.
how-check.why: You can watch every page it opens. It never clicks, types, scrolls or saves anything there.
how-check.tech: Each page has a reader set in Firebase Remote Config, so when a site changes its page, the reader can be fixed for everyone without an update.

how-understand.title: Understanding what was found
how-understand.what: Each finding says what it is, how it was found, and what removing it would do.
how-understand.why: You mark each one Mine, Not mine or Not sure. Your answer stays on this computer.
how-understand.tech: Code reads the page; Gemini Nano, on this computer, sorts each entry. Where they disagree about whose it is, Spare Key asks you.

how-plan.title: The plan
how-plan.what: An ordered list: screenshot first, talk to an advocate, then what can change now and what to leave for a better time.
how-plan.why: Changing a setting can alert the other person. The plan says which changes may be noticed, every time.
how-plan.tech: The plan is built by code from a verified steps library. Gemini in the cloud can reorder it from finding types only, and Spare Key’s safety rules check every plan before you see it.
